name: nextcore-visual-essay
description: Fast-cut, faceless visual-essay style calibrated from a breakdown of the Nextcore YouTube channel: voice-over drives everything, the image changes almost every phrase, typography and metaphor-driven cutaways carry the emotion. Default for a pure-voiceover workflow (no talking head). Copy this file per channel/series instead of editing it in place.

narrative_arc.notes: Cut when the sentence's point shifts, not when there's a pause in speech. The first frame doubles as the poster/hook — don't spend it on a logo or intro. Save the strongest emotional/cinematic footage for the escalation beat right before the conclusion, not on a throwaway line.

pacing.media_type_variety_rule: Prefer switching the underlying media TYPE (face/text/archive/object/UI) between consecutive beats over reusing the same type with a fancier transition — that's what actually resets viewer attention, not the transition itself.

composition.rule_of_one: One dominant idea per frame, readable within about a second. Collage is fine; illegibility is not.

visual_language.attention: High-contrast headline word or hero subject as the primary focal point; supporting symbols stay clearly secondary. See references/cinematic_principles.md system 1.
visual_language.depth: Collage layering (foreground symbol/object over a flatter background) substitutes for real camera depth, since there's no live camera. See system 2.
visual_language.light: Not camera-lit — 'light' means graphic contrast: a bright headline against a controlled-value background, not literal lighting direction. See system 3.
visual_language.tactility: Footage inserts can run slightly textured/imperfect (grain, soft roll-off) so they don't feel clinically flat next to clean typography frames.

color.accent_usage: Headline words, key highlights, underline/arrow accents. Never more than one accent color live on screen at once.
color.notes: Contrast matters more than color count. Footage inserts can run slightly desaturated so they read as 'texture' against cleaner graphic frames. These CDL numbers are a conservative starting push — nudge by eye against a real render.

camera_motion.avoid: Flashy 3D transitions that call attention to themselves — motion should sell the content, not the edit.

transitions.rule: The cut itself should be invisible; novelty comes from changing media type, not the transition effect.

captions.style_notes: Bold sans-serif, white with dark outline or soft drop shadow, bottom-center or lower-third. Text is a semantic highlighter, not subtitles-everywhere: one phrase -> one key word -> one typography event. Occasional single accent-color word for emphasis. Word-by-word pop-in is a Tier 2 upgrade — see references/resolve_scripting_api.md.

sound_design.foley: Light — most sources are stock/library footage without clean production audio; lean on a clip's own native sound sparingly rather than fabricating tactile detail that isn't there.
sound_design.ambience: Minimal; typography/collage frames are usually silent under the VO. Real footage inserts can keep a touch of their native ambience if it doesn't fight the voice.

music_bed.role: supports pacing, must never compete with the VO
music_bed.ducking: lower under narration — see references/beat_plan_schema.md music_bed field

sound_design.silence: Use a beat of near-silence (VO + faint bed only, no SFX) right before the escalation beat's payoff so the payoff's sound actually lands.
